Embroidery Price per 1,000 Stitches: Setting Your Rate from Machine Time

See how stitch rates interact with per-piece fees and machine speed, then test your own rate per 1,000 stitches in the calculator below.

Jump to calculator

Why Embroidery Is Priced per 1,000 Stitches

Two embroidery designs that measure the exact same width and height on a shirt can take completely different amounts of time to sew. An open line-art monogram measuring 3.5 inches wide might contain 3,000 stitches, while a full-coverage tatami patch of the same size can exceed 16,000 stitches. Because embroidery machine needle bars run at a measurable stitch speed—counted in stitches per minute (spm)—stitch count is the most direct measure of machine time and thread consumption.

However, charging only a flat rate per 1,000 stitches without a per-piece handling fee creates a trap on small designs. A 2,000-stitch name drop still requires hooping the garment, sliding it onto the machine, trimming stabilizer, andsteaming or folding. That is why the pricing formula in this tool combines a rate per 1,000 stitches with a fixed per-piece fee and a minimum decoration charge.

The Stitch-Based Pricing Formula

Using the calculator's starting values (placeholders you should customize for your own shop: $1.50 per 1,000 stitches, $1.00 per-piece fee, $5.00 minimum, and 6 included colors with $0.50 per extra color), the decoration charge before quantity breaks is:

base = (stitches ÷ 1,000) × rate + piece fee + extra-color fee × max(0, colors − colors included)

Let's compare how three different stitch counts behave at a single-piece rate (0% break) versus a 24-piece order (10% break) using those starting values, assuming 3 colors (2 color changes), 650 stitches per minute, 30 seconds per color change, and 1 minute of hooping:

  • 4,000-stitch left-chest text (3 colors):
    • Base decoration: 4 × $1.50 + $1.00 = $7.00
    • At 24 pieces (10% off): $7.00 × 0.90 = $6.30 per piece ($151.20 order total)
    • Machine time per piece: 4,000 ÷ 650 + (2 × 0.5) + 1 = 8.15 minutes
    • Effective hourly rate at 24 pieces: ($6.30 ÷ 8.15) × 60 = $46.38/hr
  • 8,000-stitch cap logo (Worked Example 1, 3 colors):
    • Base decoration: 8 × $1.50 + $1.00 = $13.00
    • At 24 pieces (10% off): $13.00 × 0.90 = $11.70 per piece ($280.80 order total)
    • Machine time per piece: 8,000 ÷ 650 + (2 × 0.5) + 1 = 14.31 minutes
    • Effective hourly rate at 24 pieces: ($11.70 ÷ 14.31) × 60 = $49.06/hr
  • 15,000-stitch dense emblem (3 colors):
    • Base decoration: 15 × $1.50 + $1.00 = $23.50
    • At 24 pieces (10% off): $23.50 × 0.90 = $21.15 per piece ($507.60 order total)
    • Machine time per piece: 15,000 ÷ 650 + (2 × 0.5) + 1 = 25.08 minutes
    • Effective hourly rate at 24 pieces: ($21.15 ÷ 25.08) × 60 = $50.60/hr

Notice how pairing the $1.50 stitch rate with the $1.00 per-piece hooping fee keeps the effective hourly rate remarkably steady across all three design sizes—ranging from $46.38/hr on the 4,000-stitch design to $50.60/hr on the 15,000-stitch design.

How to Back-Calculate Your Own Rate per 1,000 Stitches

Instead of copying another shop's price chart without knowing their equipment or overhead, you can derive your own rate per 1,000 stitches from three numbers you already know:

  1. Your real average stitching speed: Time a representative design on your machine from start to finish. If an 8,000-stitch design with 2 color changes takes 13 minutes and 18 seconds of machine run time (excluding hooping), and the 2 color changes took 1 minute total, your active sewing speed is roughly 8,000 ÷ 12.31 = 650 stitches per minute.
  2. Your handling and hooping time per piece: Measure how long it takes you to hoop a garment, load and unload the frame, and trim backing. If hooping occurs while a single-head machine is stopped between garments, enter the full handling time (for example, 1.0 to 2.0 minutes). If you hoop on a second set of frames while the machine is actively sewing, enter only the frame swap time (for example, 0.25 to 0.5 minutes).
  3. Your target revenue per machine hour: Decide what one machine head needs to earn per hour to cover your labor, thread, backing, needles, power, and profit margin.

Suppose you run a single-head machine at 650 stitches per minute and want to earn roughly $60.00/hr on a 24-piece order (where a 10% discount applies) for an 8,000-stitch, 3-color design (14.31 minutes per piece):

  • To earn $60.00/hr over a 14.31-minute cycle, the discounted decoration price per piece needs to be (14.31 ÷ 60) × $60.00 = $14.31.
  • Before the 10% break at 24 pieces, that corresponds to a base price of $14.31 ÷ 0.90 = $15.90.
  • If your per-piece hooping fee is $1.50, the remaining $14.40 comes from 8 thousand stitches: $14.40 ÷ 8 = $1.80 per 1,000 stitches.

You can test this directly in the calculator above: open Shop Rate Settings & Machine Speed, set Rate per 1,000 Stitches to $1.80 and Per-Piece Fee to $1.50, and watch the 24-piece effective hourly rate update to $60.00/hr ($14.31 per piece, $343.44 order total).

Single-Head vs. Multi-Head Order Run Time

The calculator tracks both minutes per piece and order machine time:

order machine time = (minutes per piece × quantity) ÷ heads

In Worked Example 1, 24 caps at 14.31 minutes per cap require 343.38 minutes on a 1-head machine. If you run the same 24 caps on a 4-head machine (heads = 4), all four heads stitch simultaneously in 6 runs of 4 caps, cutting total machine run time to 343.38 ÷ 4 = 85.85 minutes while generating the same $280.80 order total.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why not use a sliding scale where the rate per 1,000 stitches drops as stitch count increases?

Combining a fixed per-piece handling fee (such as $1.00 or $2.00) with a flat rate per 1,000 stitches automatically produces a higher effective rate per 1,000 stitches on small designs and a lower effective rate per 1,000 stitches on large designs—without maintaining a complicated multi-axis lookup chart.

What happens when a design has very few stitches, like a 1,500-stitch monogram?

At starting values, 1,500 stitches plus a $1.00 piece fee equals $3.25. Because $3.25 is below the $5.00 minimum per piece, the calculator enforces the $5.00 minimum decoration charge.

Does the rate per 1,000 stitches include the blank shirt or cap?

No. The stitch rate covers decoration only. Blank garment cost and your garment markup percentage are calculated separately and added to the decoration price to form the total per-piece price.

144-Pack Pre-Wound 60 wt L-Style Bobbins

Fewer Thread Breaks

100-Pack 75/11 Titanium Nitride Needles

Titanium coating resists adhesive buildup and heat at 650–850+ spm, cutting thread-break stops.

Bulk Cutaway Roll

2.5 oz Cutaway Stabilizer (100-Yard Roll)

Buying cutaway backing by the roll instead of pre-cut sheets cuts per-hooping stabilizer cost in half.

Faster Hooping Cycles

Temporary Embroidery Mist Adhesive (505-Style)

Holds backing and applique fabric in place during framing to shave seconds off your hooping time per piece.

Machine Speed Maintenance

Clear Sewing & Embroidery Rotary Hook Oil

One drop on the rotary hook race every 4–8 hours of stitching prevents friction and thread shredding.

Tip: Keep consumable costs (backing, thread, bobbin, and needle wear—typically $0.15–$0.35 per piece) covered inside your per-piece hooping and handling fee.
